summary: vanexa-agent daemon executes remote-controlled shell commands via hardcoded WebSocket relay
details: When `vanexa-agent start` is run, the daemon opens a WebSocket to a hardcoded third-party relay at `vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev` (a Cloudflare Workers deployment) and processes messages from that relay as commands. `task_request` messages spawn an AgentLoop whose `terminal.exec` tool calls `spawn('/bin/bash', ['-c', args.command])` with the command string supplied by the remote peer, giving anyone who can send messages on the relay session shell execution on the host. `config_update` messages are merged into the on-disk config and can flip `grantAllAccess=true`, disable approval gating, and expand `workspacePaths` to arbitrary filesystem roots, so a remote peer can escalate the shell primitive into unattended full-host RCE with broadened filesystem reach. The relay hostname is also force-migrated over any previously configured `vanexa-agent-relay.workers.dev` value. The tool-invocation path is gated only by a 6-digit pairing session id used as the WebSocket path, and all trust in the tool-execution path is anchored in whoever operates that Worker.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
